cards.title: Three-part story
cards.text: Every story has a beginning (who and where), a turn (something changes) and an ending (what it means).

cards.title: Start in the moment
cards.text: Open in the middle of action: “The lights went out, and the whole bus fell silent.”

cards.title: Show, don’t tell
cards.text: Instead of “I was scared”, say “My hands went cold and my voice vanished.”

options: My hands went cold and my voice vanished

cards.title: One character, one wish
cards.text: A story grabs us when someone wants something and something stands in the way.

qs.q: A story grips us when a character…
options: Wants something and faces an obstacle

cards.title: Add a ticking clock
cards.text: A deadline, like “the bus leaves in five minutes”, makes listeners lean in.

cards.title: The rule of three
cards.text: Three attempts, three clues or three steps feel complete: two feels short, four drags.

cards.title: Twist ending
cards.text: A twist reveals something that changes how we see everything before, like the stranger being a long-lost sister.

options: Changes how we see the story

cards.title: End with meaning
cards.text: Finish with what the story taught or changed, not just “and then I went home”.

cards.title: Dialogue brings life
cards.text: One line of speech, like “Don’t open it,” she whispered, makes characters feel real.

cards.title: Small details, big feeling
cards.text: A cracked cup or a muddy shoe tells more than a long description.

cards.title: Give names
cards.text: Naming the dog “Biscuit” or the street “Mango Lane” makes it feel true.

cards.title: Change the pace
cards.text: Short sentences speed things up. Long ones slow down and let feelings settle.

cards.title: Mystery hooks
cards.text: Start with a question the listener wants answered: “Why did the clock stop at 3:15?”

cards.title: Circle back
cards.text: End by echoing your first line. It gives a satisfying, finished feeling.

options: Echoing your opening at the end

cards.title: Five senses
cards.text: Describe what you see, hear, smell, taste and touch. Most speakers only use sight.

qs.q: Which sense do speakers forget most?

cards.title: Simile
cards.text: A simile compares using ‘like’ or ‘as’: “silence as heavy as a wet blanket”.

cards.title: Metaphor
cards.text: A metaphor says one thing is another: “The classroom was a beehive.”

qs.q: “The city is a jungle” is a…

cards.title: Be specific
cards.text: Say “a rusty green bicycle” rather than “a bicycle”. Specific words paint pictures.

cards.title: Strong verbs
cards.text: “She stormed in” beats “She walked in angrily”. A strong verb replaces a weak verb and an adverb.

options: He went fast down the lane

cards.title: Sound words
cards.text: Words like crackle, hiss and thud let listeners hear the scene.

cards.title: Colour and light
cards.text: Light sets the mood: golden evening, flickering candle, harsh white tube-light.

cards.title: Weather as mood
cards.text: Rain feels sad or calm, bright sun feels hopeful. Weather mirrors feelings.

qs.q: A stormy sky often hints at…

cards.title: Use contrast
cards.text: “Tiny hands, enormous courage.” Opposites make a line memorable.

cards.title: Personification
cards.text: Giving things human feelings: “The old clock sighed and stopped.”

cards.title: Zoom in
cards.text: Pick one tiny thing, like a drop sliding down a window, and describe it closely.

cards.title: Avoid cliché
cards.text: Phrases like “quiet as a mouse” are tired. Invent your own picture.

cards.title: Adjective diet
cards.text: Two sharp adjectives beat five vague ones. “Cold, metallic smell”.

cards.title: Rhythm
cards.text: Read a line aloud. If it trips your tongue, simplify it.

qs.q: Reading a line aloud helps you…

cards.title: If this continues…
cards.text: Take something true today and push it forward: “If screens keep growing, what happens to conversation?”

options: Extends a trend into the future

cards.title: Hopeful and worried
cards.text: A balanced future talk shows both hopes and dangers, not just one.

cards.title: Future of work
cards.text: Many jobs may change with AI and automation. Skills like creativity and teamwork stay valuable.

cards.title: Future cities
cards.text: Imagine smart traffic, rooftop farms, quiet electric streets and clean air.

qs.q: A clean future city might use…

cards.title: Future home
cards.text: Homes may be energy-saving and voice-controlled. Ask: what stays the same, such as family and food?

qs.q: What may stay the same in the future?

cards.title: Future school
cards.text: Classrooms may include virtual field trips and personal AI tutors, while teachers guide and inspire.

qs.q: A future teacher’s key role is…

cards.title: Future health
cards.text: Early detection, telemedicine and personalised medicine could help more people live well.

cards.title: Future food
cards.text: Vertical farms, lab-grown food and less waste could feed a growing world.

qs.q: A way to feed more people is…

cards.title: Future earth
cards.text: Cleaner energy, rewilding and recycling could make the planet healthier for our grandchildren.

cards.title: Future travel
cards.text: Faster trains, electric flights and virtual visits may change how we explore.

cards.title: Future self
cards.text: When you speak about yourself in 50 years, mention work, family, place, and the values you kept.

cards.title: Time words
cards.text: Use time markers: “By 2075…”, “In my grandchildren’s time…”, “Decades from now…”.

cards.title: Warn and inspire
cards.text: End a future talk with a call: “The future is not something we enter; it is something we create.”

cards.title: Sci-fi isn’t silly
cards.text: Many modern ideas, such as video calls, started as science fiction. Imagination sparks invention.

cards.title: Name the feeling
cards.text: Pick a precise word: not “sad” but “lonely”, “disappointed” or “homesick”.

cards.title: Courage
cards.text: Courage is not the absence of fear; it is acting even when afraid.

cards.title: Friendship
cards.text: True friends listen, help, tell the truth kindly and stay through hard times.

cards.title: Kindness
cards.text: Small kindnesses, like a smile or sharing lunch, can change someone’s whole day.

cards.title: Gratitude
cards.text: Saying thank you, and meaning it, makes both people happier.

cards.title: Fear
cards.text: Fear warns us of danger. Talking about it makes it smaller.

cards.title: Loneliness
cards.text: Even in a crowd, one can feel lonely. A message or a smile can help.

cards.title: Forgiveness
cards.text: Forgiving someone does not mean what they did was okay; it frees you from carrying anger.

cards.title: Family
cards.text: Family can be those we are born into or those we choose, who care for us.

cards.title: Empathy
cards.text: Empathy is imagining how someone else feels. It is the root of kindness.

cards.title: Body shows feeling
cards.text: Shaking hands, a tight jaw, a wide smile: describe the body to show the feeling.

cards.title: Regret
cards.text: Regret is a feeling about something we wish we had done differently. It can be a teacher.

cards.title: Joy
cards.text: Joy is often found in simple moments: tea with family, rain on the roof, a goal scored.

cards.title: Respect
cards.text: Respect means treating every person as important, whatever their role.

cards.title: Pick one moment
cards.text: Instead of “my life”, tell one real moment, like the day you got lost in a market.

qs.q: A personal speech works best with…

cards.title: Lesson at the end
cards.text: After the story, say what you learnt: “I realised asking for help is strength.”

qs.q: A personal story should end with…

cards.title: Be honest
cards.text: Honesty makes listeners trust you. Admit nerves or mistakes.

cards.title: Use ‘I’
cards.text: In a personal topic, speak in first person. It is your story.

cards.title: Add humour
cards.text: A small funny detail relaxes the room: “My bicycle had more courage than I did.”

cards.title: Describe a person
cards.text: Pick two traits and one habit: “my grandmother, patient, stubborn, always humming.”

cards.title: Favourite place
cards.text: Use senses: what you hear, smell and feel there, and why it matters to you.

qs.q: To describe a favourite place, include…

cards.title: Dreams
cards.text: Explain not just what you dream of but why, and the first small step you take.

cards.title: Turning point
cards.text: Tell what happened before, the event itself, and how you changed after.

cards.title: Mistakes teach
cards.text: Speaking about a mistake shows maturity. Say what you would do differently.

cards.title: Proud moments
cards.text: Explain the effort behind your pride, not just the result.

qs.q: A proud story is stronger with…

cards.title: Values
cards.text: Name two or three values you live by, such as honesty and curiosity, and give an example.

cards.title: Talk to one person
cards.text: Imagine you are speaking to one friend. It makes personal speeches warm.

qs.q: Imagining one friend helps you sound…

cards.title: Small is powerful
cards.text: A tiny habit, like writing three lines each night, can make a rich story.

cards.title: Define first
cards.text: Start an abstract topic by defining the key word in your own way: “To me, luck is…”.

cards.title: Both sides
cards.text: Show two views before choosing: “Some say… others believe…”.

qs.q: Showing both sides makes you sound…

cards.title: Use an analogy
cards.text: Compare the idea to something familiar: “Habits are like footprints in wet cement.”

qs.q: An analogy explains an idea by…

cards.title: Thought experiment
cards.text: Ask “what if…?” to test an idea: what if nobody could lie for a day?

cards.title: Example, not statistics
cards.text: For big ideas, a short real example convinces better than numbers.

qs.q: To make an idea real, use…

cards.title: Why before what
cards.text: Explain why something matters before explaining what it is.

cards.title: Paradox
cards.text: A paradox seems contradictory but holds truth: “The more you give, the more you have.”

cards.title: Quote wisely
cards.text: One short quote, explained in your own words, is enough. Do not stack many.

qs.q: A quote works best when you…

cards.title: Question openers
cards.text: Ask a question that you answer later: “Is silence empty?”

cards.title: Pros and cons
cards.text: For ideas like technology, list one gain and one loss, then decide.

qs.q: After pros and cons, you should…

cards.title: Personal angle
cards.text: Connect an abstract idea to your own life to make it real.

qs.q: A personal angle makes an idea…

cards.title: Reasons then conclusion
cards.text: State your view, give two or three reasons, and restate. This keeps the talk clear.

cards.title: Avoid extremes
cards.text: Words like always and never are rarely true. Use often and sometimes.

cards.title: Ask who benefits
cards.text: When judging an idea, ask who gains and who loses. It reveals depth.

cards.title: Notice the ordinary
cards.text: “A day without…” topics ask what we usually take for granted, from water to light.

qs.q: ‘A day without…’ topics ask you to…
options: Notice what we take for granted

cards.title: Morning to night
cards.text: Walk through the day: wake up, travel, school, evening. Say what is missing at each point.

cards.title: What we miss
cards.text: Absence shows value: only without music do we notice how much it fills a day.

cards.title: Silence
cards.text: Without speaking, you notice gestures, eyes, birdsong and what people mean without saying.

cards.title: Without phones
cards.text: Imagine conversations at the dinner table, long walks and boredom that turns into ideas.

qs.q: A day without phones might bring…

cards.title: Without electricity
cards.text: Candles, hand fans, cold water and stories in the dark. Mention what is lost and what is gained.

cards.title: Without school
cards.text: Free time feels great, but friends, learning and routine are missed.

cards.title: Without rules
cards.text: Rules protect us. Without them, strong people may take over and the weak suffer.

cards.title: Without lying
cards.text: Honest days may hurt a little but build real trust.

qs.q: A world without lies would build…

cards.title: Without water
cards.text: Water touches everything: drinking, cooking, farming. A day without it shows how precious it is.

cards.title: Compare then and now
cards.text: Contrast with how people lived long ago: they managed with less and talked more.

cards.title: End with gratitude
cards.text: Finish by thanking the things we usually ignore.

qs.q: A good ending for these topics is…

cards.title: Use contrast words
cards.text: But, however, yet, instead: they help show the before and after.

cards.title: Feelings through the day
cards.text: Track feelings: curious in the morning, bored by noon, grateful at night.

cards.title: Pause is power
cards.text: A one-second pause before a key line makes it land. Silence feels long to you, short to them.

cards.title: Slow down
cards.text: Nerves speed us up. Breathe and speak a little slower than feels natural.

cards.title: Eye contact
cards.text: Look at one person for a full thought, then move to another.

cards.title: Strong opening
cards.text: Memorise your first sentence. A confident start settles the nerves.

cards.title: If you blank
cards.text: Pause, breathe, repeat your last line, or say “Let me put it another way.”

qs.q: If you blank out, you can…
options: Pause and repeat your last line

cards.title: Vary your voice
cards.text: Change volume and pace. A monotone voice loses people fast.

cards.title: Use your hands
cards.text: Natural gestures support words. Keep them open, avoid fidgeting.

cards.title: Posture
cards.text: Stand tall with feet apart. Standing well makes you feel and sound more confident.

cards.title: Filler words
cards.text: Replace ‘um’ and ‘like’ with a silent pause. It sounds calm.

cards.title: Plan in 60 seconds
cards.text: Pick a hook, a stance, two points and an ending. Write a few keywords only.

cards.title: Signpost
cards.text: Say “first”, “next”, “finally” so listeners can follow.

cards.title: Smile
cards.text: A smile in the voice makes you sound friendlier, even on serious topics.

cards.title: Nerves are normal
cards.text: Nerves give you energy. Even experienced speakers feel them.

cards.title: Time awareness
cards.text: For three minutes, aim for hook (20 s), 2–3 points (2 min), and ending (30 s).

cards.title: Why we dream
cards.text: Scientists think dreams help the brain sort memories and feelings during sleep.

cards.title: Sleep matters
cards.text: Sleep helps memory, mood and growth. Teens need more than adults.

cards.title: Memory
cards.text: Memory is not a recording; each recall slightly rebuilds the memory.

cards.title: Time is relative
cards.text: Time feels slow when we are bored and fast when we enjoy ourselves.

qs.q: Time feels fast when we are…

cards.title: Our tiny planet
cards.text: From space, Earth looks small and borderless, which many astronauts say changes their view.

qs.q: Seeing Earth from space makes many feel…

cards.title: Stars are old
cards.text: Starlight takes years to reach us, so we see stars as they were long ago.

qs.q: Starlight shows stars as they were…

cards.title: Animals communicate
cards.text: Whales sing, bees dance and ants leave scent trails to share information.

cards.title: Languages
cards.text: Thousands of languages exist; each carries a different way of seeing the world.

options: A way of seeing the world

cards.title: Colour perception
cards.text: People see colours differently; some cannot tell red from green, which is called colour blindness.

cards.title: Why we laugh
cards.text: Laughter connects people and releases tension, even among strangers.

cards.title: Bridges and builders
cards.text: Bridges connect places and cultures. Builders usually imagined the connection before it existed.

qs.q: A bridge is often a symbol of…

cards.title: Sound of silence
cards.text: Truly silent places are rare. Even a quiet room has hums and heartbeat.

cards.title: Mirrors
cards.text: Mirrors flip left and right but not up and down. They show us ourselves but not how others see us.

cards.title: Clocks and calendars
cards.text: Humans invented clocks and calendars to share time, based on the Sun and the Moon.
